audit: Qwen3.6-27B C512 shape-specialized large-M projection dataflow

scope.purpose: Bind Gate/Up and Down decisions to the pinned layer-0 checkpoint payload, test the horizontal M128N256 NVFP4 topology rather than extrapolating from Gate-only synthetic microbenchmarks, and close the public Down-module/autotune evidence gap.

live_checkpoint_bridge.production_prefill_execution: eager; module Graph-safe but Prefill graph capture is not implemented

horizontal_p0.mapping: one 512-thread CTA; two horizontal 8-warp M128N128 groups; common two-slot A; private two-slot B/scale; CTA-wide steady-state barrier
horizontal_p0.decision: reject from production; retain as the exact resource/correctness sentinel for the horizontal topology

horizontal_named_p1.mapping: P0 arithmetic plus raw SM80 mbarrier ready/free phases for common A and private B; alternate A producer subgroup
horizontal_named_p1.decision: reject; per-stage multi-barrier control costs more than the recovered subgroup phase independence

context_autotune_reliability.old_failure: a fixed 5.0 ms winner threshold treated frequency and contention as permanent route unavailability
context_autotune_reliability.new_protocol: two interleaved warmup rounds, three interleaved timing rounds with two iterations each, best valid sample; failed heuristics are discarded independently

down.decision: retain the already-integrated exact-C512 production Down bridge; its public module now has direct pinned-payload evidence and its factory no longer silently disables the route under transient contention

conclusions: Gate/Up and Down require separate runtime cells; the real checkpoint confirms that their best current implementations are not the same native tile configuration.
Combining A reuse and B decode reuse inside one 512-thread Gate CTA is resource-feasible and exact, but both full-CTA and per-stage mbarrier schedules regress latency.
The 512-thread result rejects this concrete synchronization structure, not the general goal of coupled operand reuse.
Down already clears the production performance gate with its shape-specific bridge, is integrated independently from Gate/Up, and should not wait for a future native Gate kernel.
FP8 QKV/Z/O remains a separate backend family because it has no NVFP4 decode stage; it may reuse selector and scheduling infrastructure only.
next_actions: add Gate/Up and Down production route readiness/hit/fallback observability while preserving their independent exact-C512 selectors; both bridges are already integrated
keep absolute performance gates in repeatable ceiling/CI tests rather than production context availability checks
treat Prefill CUDA Graph and OpenAI-compatible API/eval harness work as separate usability and launch-overhead tracks; current production Prefill is eager

for the next native Gate skeleton, avoid per-K64 multi-mbarrier control and evaluate a design that preserves independent 256-thread CTA phasing while treating A reuse as an L2/locality scheduling problem
refresh production NSys projection ranking before starting separate FP8 QKV/Z/O cells
